_purpose: Canonical SASB FN-CB Commercial Banks topic schema (2025-12 version).
_used_by: pipeline/stage1_*.py and pipeline/stage2_score.py (loaded by Stage 1.2 retrieval and Stage 2 prompt rendering; same schema for Claude and GPT)

data_security.name: Data Security
data_security.summary: Ensuring personal financial data privacy and security is an essential responsibility of Commercial Banks. Entities that fail to safeguard customer data may be susceptible to decreased revenue and consumer confidence. As the growth in mobile banking and cloud storage continues and more bank operations become technology- and internet-dependent, data security management becomes increasingly important. Sophisticated technology and continuous staff training are essential amid growing cybersecurity threats.

metrics.description: (1) Number of data breaches, (2) percentage that are personal data breaches, (3) number of account holders affected
Description of approach to identifying and addressing data security risks (including emerging cyber threats, attack vectors, regulatory environment)

evidence_required_for_high_score: explicit count of breaches in the year
percentage that involved personal data
number of customers affected
description of cyber risk identification and response process
discussion of emerging threat landscape

financial_inclusion.name: Financial Inclusion & Capacity Building
financial_inclusion.summary: As their primary business activity, commercial banks must continuously balance their capacity building efforts with the risks and opportunities associated with lending to unbanked, underbanked or underserved customers. Emerging financing models and technologies provide banks with an opportunity to offer products and services in previously underserved markets and obtain additional sources of revenue.

metrics.description: (1) Number and (2) amount of loans outstanding that qualify for programmes designed to promote small business and community development
(1) Number and (2) amount of past due and nonaccrual loans or loans subject to forbearance that qualify for programmes designed to promote small business and community development
Number of no-cost retail checking accounts provided to previously unbanked or underbanked customers
Number of participants in financial literacy initiatives for unbanked, underbanked, or underserved customers

evidence_required_for_high_score: number/amount of loans to small business / community development programmes
number of no-cost accounts opened for underbanked customers
number of financial literacy participants
description of strategy linking results back into product design

esg_credit_analysis.name: Incorporation of Environmental, Social, and Governance Factors in Credit Analysis
esg_credit_analysis.summary: As financial intermediaries, commercial banks contribute to significant positive and negative environmental and social externalities through their lending practices. ESG factors can have material implications for the underlying entities, assets and projects to which commercial banks lend. Banks must examine ESG factors when determining the quality of collateral and may enable positive externalities through ESG-aligned lending.

metrics.description: Commercial and industrial credit exposure, by industry
Description of approach to incorporation of ESG factors in credit analysis (including parties responsible, oversight, accountability, integration into creditworthiness assessment)

evidence_required_for_high_score: industry-by-industry credit exposure breakdown
named ESG-in-credit framework / policy
description of governance roles and oversight bodies
description of how ESG factors enter the credit decision

financed_emissions.name: Financed Emissions
financed_emissions.summary: Entities participating in commercial banking activities face risks and opportunities related to the greenhouse gas emissions associated with those activities. Counterparties with higher emissions might be more susceptible to risks associated with technological changes, supply and demand shifts and policy change, which in turn can impact the prospects of the financial institution providing services to these entities. These risks can arise as credit risk, market risk, reputational risk.

metrics.description: Absolute gross financed emissions, disaggregated by (1) Scope 1, (2) Scope 2 and (3) Scope 3
Gross exposure for each industry by asset class (financed emissions disclosure under IFRS S2 B62-B62A)
Percentage of gross exposure included in the financed emissions calculation
Description of the methodology used to calculate financed emissions

evidence_required_for_high_score: absolute Scope 1/2/3 financed emissions numbers
industry/sector breakdown of exposure
% of gross exposure covered by the calculation
named methodology (PCAF) and explanation

business_ethics.name: Business Ethics
business_ethics.summary: The regulatory environment surrounding the Commercial Banks industry continues to evolve internationally. Entities must adhere to a complex and often inconsistent set of rules relating to performance and conduct, as well as provide disclosure on issues including insider trading, antitrust behaviour, price fixing and market manipulation. Entities are subject to strict legal requirements against tax evasion, fraud, money laundering and corrupt practices.

metrics.description: Total amount of monetary losses as a result of legal proceedings associated with fraud, insider trading, antitrust, anti-competitive behaviour, market manipulation, malpractice, or other related financial industry laws or regulations
Description of whistleblower policies and procedures

evidence_required_for_high_score: monetary losses from legal proceedings (with $ amount)
context of those losses (fraud / antitrust / etc.)
description of whistleblower policy and reporting channels
corrective actions taken

systemic_risk.name: Systemic Risk Management
systemic_risk.summary: Commercial Bank entities that fail to manage risks to capital effectively may suffer significant losses while increasing their liabilities. Because of the interconnectedness of the global financial system, these failures can contribute to significant market disruption and financial crises. The systemic interconnectedness of financial institutions has become a central concern for regulators. Many jurisdictions require that banks undergo supervised stress tests to evaluate whether the entity has sufficient capital reserves and liquidity to absorb shocks.

metrics.description: Global Systemically Important Bank (G-SIB) score, by category
Description of approach to incorporation of results of mandatory and voluntary stress tests into capital adequacy planning, long-term corporate strategy, and other business activities

evidence_required_for_high_score: G-SIB / D-SIB score (or explicit statement that bank is not designated)
regulatory capital ratios (CET1, leverage)
description of stress test scenarios and integration into planning
description of recovery / resolution arrangements

applicability_rules._purpose: Some report types do not address all 6 topics. a_i = 0 if the topic is out of scope for the report TYPE.
